items.q: A new image is made with Image.new('RGBA', (10, 10)) and no colour. What does getpixel((0, 0)) return?
rationales: Opaque black is the default of an RGB image; an RGBA image starts with alpha 0.
Pillow does not start from white.

items.q: Table 21-1 of the chapter gives Green as (0, 255, 0, 255). What does ImageColor.getcolor('green', 'RGBA') return?
rationales: That is the colour of 'lime', the HTML name of full green; the table has one wrong row.
'green' is in Pillow's table of 148 names.

items.q: What is the size of im.crop((10, 5, 40, 35)) for a 60 by 40 image?
options: (30, 30), because the right and bottom edges are left out
rationales: A box includes its left and top edge and excludes its right and bottom edge.
The box tuple holds corners, not a size: the width is 40 minus 10.

items.q: An RGBA image is saved with im.save('card.jpg'). What happens?
options: A JPEG is written and the transparency is kept
An OSError, 'cannot write mode RGBA as JPEG'
The file is written as a PNG with the .jpg name
rationales: JPEG has no alpha channel, so there is nothing to keep it in.
Pillow chooses the format from the extension and does not rename it.

items.q: What does a.paste(b, (0, 0)) return, and what has happened to a?
options: A new image that holds the result; a is unchanged
None; a itself has been changed
rationales: crop() and resize() return new images, but paste() works on its own image.
paste() returns nothing; it copies b into a.

items.q: A white RGB image is rotated with im.rotate(30). What colour are the corners that no pixel reaches?
options: White, the colour of the picture
rationales: The fill does not copy the picture's colour.
Transparent is the fill of an RGBA image; an RGB image has no alpha, so the fill is black.

items.q: The batch program skips every name that does not end in the lower case .png or .jpg. Which of a.png, C.PNG, d.jpeg and n.txt does it process?
rationales: The test is case sensitive, so C.PNG is skipped.
The extension .jpeg is not .jpg, so d.jpeg is skipped as well.

items.q: draw.rectangle((20, 30, 60, 60), fill='red') is called on a black image. How many red pixels are there?
options: 1271 is wrong; the last pixel is left out, so 1160
rationales: That is the crop() arithmetic; a drawn rectangle includes its last pixel.
Unlike crop(), ImageDraw includes the last pixel.

items.q: The 2nd edition used draw.textsize() to measure text. Which calls does Pillow 12 offer instead?
rationales: It was removed in Pillow 10.0.0.
getsize() of fonts was removed in the same release.
The figure is reached with plt.gcf(); plot() returns the lines it drew.
plot() draws and returns the lines; show() is the one that returns None.

items.q: In one program plt.plot() is called twice and then plt.show() with the Agg backend. How many lines does plt.gca() hold afterwards?
options: 2, because pyplot keeps the current figure and show() does not clear it with Agg
1, because the second call replaces the first
rationales: With a window, closing it ends the figure; Agg shows nothing and leaves the figure.
Every plot call adds to the current axes.
